concepts.def: Who actually pays a tax — buyer or seller.
Inelastic goods bear most tax on consumer.
Tax on cigarettes, alcohol to deter use.
Demand more elastic in long run.
% change in demand for X ÷ % change in price of Y.

walkthroughs.body_html: When demand is inelastic (cigarettes), firms can pass the tax onto consumers — buyers bear most. When demand is elastic, consumers walk away, so firms swallow more of the tax. That's why governments target inelastic goods for revenue.

A train company with monopoly routes (inelastic) pushes peak fares up. A small coffee shop in a busy street (elastic — substitutes everywhere) competes by lowering price. Smart firms estimate PED before changing prices.

PED estimates aren't perfect. They change over time, vary by income level, and depend on the size of the price change. Always mention: 'However, PED may differ in the long run as consumers find substitutes.'
